{"id": "2514ccdc-03cd-4588-bc43-de354c75193a", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Confirmed — this is almost certainly the root cause. **Kubernetes 1.32 is the last version for which EKS releases AL2 AMIs.** There is no AL2 AMI build for 1.33 at all, so a managed node group on 1.33 using an AL2 AMI either:
- can't find/launch a valid AMI for that version, or
- if a stale/pinned AL2 AMI (built for an older control-plane minor) is being used via a custom launch template, the kubelet version mismatches the 1.33 control plane and fails to register — producing `NodeCreationFailure`.

That cleanly explains why your 1.32 node group is fine and the new 1.33 one isn't — it's not a networking/IAM/bootstrap issue, it's an AMI compatibility wall.

Let me run this through the dedicated node-join diagnostic to confirm against your actual cluster/node group config (in case there's a secondary issue layered on top), then give you the fix.", "type": "text"}, {"id": "tooluse_bGV7WE6JIQTuST4mp6KOq1", "tool_name": "skill_read", "input": {"skill_id": "eks-node-join-diagnostic"}, "type": "tool_use", "display_intent": "Load EKS node join diagnostic skill to check cluster config."}], "created_at": null}

Use this routing:\\\\n\\\\n**Fast path** \\\\u2014 If the symptom directly maps to a known root cause with high\\\\nconfidence (e.g., user says \\\\\"I have a pathed role ARN in aws-auth\\\\\"), identify\\\\nthe root cause immediately, then validate with only the relevant subset of\\\\nchecks (the specific NJ ID + its prerequisites).
